subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw core grow a runtime-enforced artifact-gated anti-drift state machine for agent runs, or should the existing narrower tool-loop/stuck-session/strict-agentic guards remain the intended boundary for now?
rationale: The request adds broad runtime policy, persistence, thresholds, telemetry, and a feature flag; automation cannot choose the product boundary or upgrade-safe state model from the issue text alone.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed core design
options.body: Design the guard around existing runtime/task lifecycle and SQLite-backed state, then split implementation into focused PRs with live reproductions and tuning evidence.

options.title: Keep current partial guards
options.body: Leave tool-loop detection, stuck-session diagnostics, strict-agentic recovery, and subagent completion checks as the supported guardrails until concrete failures justify more enforcement.

options.title: Route CI-green batching elsewhere
options.body: If the no-idle-after-green requirement is only about ClawSweeper or maintainer automation batches, track that in the automation owner repo instead of OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed core design
recommendation.body: Design the guard around existing runtime/task lifecycle and SQLite-backed state, then split implementation into focused PRs with live reproductions and tuning evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete appears repeatedly in recent agent-runtime and lifecycle history and is the best available routing candidate for a broad core policy decision.
